classification.difficultyReason: Solve parameter problems with an auxiliary scalar and explain algebraically and geometrically why the parallel condition is independent of the chosen nonzero multiple.

children.label: a
children.prompt:
Find the value of $p$ such that $p\underset{\sim}{a}+\underset{\sim}{b}$ is parallel to $\begin{pmatrix}7\\2\end{pmatrix}$.

Remember that parallel means $p\underset{\sim}{a}+\underset{\sim}{b}=k\begin{pmatrix}7\\2\end{pmatrix}$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Explain algebraically why the value of $p$ does not depend on the scalar multiple of $\begin{pmatrix}7\\2\end{pmatrix}$.

answer.short: Any nonzero scalar multiplying the target vector is absorbed into $k$, so the equation determining $p$ is unchanged.
answer.worked:
For a nonzero scalar $r$, write
$$\begin{aligned}\begin{pmatrix}3p+1\\-2p+4\end{pmatrix}&=k\left(r\begin{pmatrix}7\\2\end{pmatrix}\right)\\3p+1&=7kr\\-2p+4&=2kr\end{aligned}$$
Eliminating $kr$ gives $2(3p+1)=7(-2p+4)$, the same equation as in part a. Hence $p=\frac{13}{10}$ is unchanged.

answer.short: Nonzero scalar multiples point in the same or opposite direction, so they all give the same parallel condition.
answer.worked: Multiplying $\begin{pmatrix}7\\2\end{pmatrix}$ by a nonzero scalar changes its magnitude and may reverse its direction. Its line of direction stays the same. Therefore the value of $p$ needed for parallelism is unchanged.

children.label: d
children.prompt: Find the value of $q$ such that $\underset{\sim}{a}+q\underset{\sim}{b}$ is perpendicular to $\begin{pmatrix}5\\1\end{pmatrix}$.

answer.worked:
$$\underset{\sim}{a}+q\underset{\sim}{b}=\begin{pmatrix}3+q\\-2+4q\end{pmatrix}$$
A vector perpendicular to $\begin{pmatrix}5\\1\end{pmatrix}$ is parallel to $\begin{pmatrix}1\\-5\end{pmatrix}$ or $\begin{pmatrix}-1\\5\end{pmatrix}$.
Using $\begin{pmatrix}1\\-5\end{pmatrix}$:
$$\begin{aligned}\begin{pmatrix}3+q\\-2+4q\end{pmatrix}&=k\begin{pmatrix}1\\-5\end{pmatrix}\\3+q&=k\\-2+4q&=-5k\end{aligned}$$
Substitute $k=3+q$:
$$\begin{aligned}-2+4q&=-5(3+q)\\-2+4q&=-15-5q\\9q&=-13\\q&=-\frac{13}{9}\end{aligned}$$
There is only one solution; using the opposite perpendicular direction gives the same value of $q$.
